metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; adjust downward bias by 2–5% for periods with high recent volatility.
- Overshoots occur after spikes (e.g., 48.25, 49.61) — model overreacts and peaks too early; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) — no behavioral signal to override technical patterns; treat as neutral baseline.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often lag true price movements by 2–4 days; shift forecast 1–2 days forward if price is trending upward.
- Avoid overfitting to recent low prices — if last 3–5 days are below 40, don’t assume continuation; add 5–10% buffer for rebound potential.
